Natural-active skincare with dual-action technology:
calm chronic inflammation and restore healthy skin at every use
home.prod.label: The ALFURIN Range
home.prod.sub: Formulated together for daily use — the lotion and cream work in combination to soothe, protect, and restore psoriatic-prone skin.
home.story.label: Daily Ritual
home.story.p: ALFURIN is designed to fit seamlessly into your daily routine. A non-greasy, dermatologically tested formula that leaves skin calm and protected from the very first application — no harsh ingredients, no compromise.
home.step1.title: Cleanse
home.step1.p: Gently clean affected areas with lukewarm water. Pat dry with a soft towel.
home.step2.title: Apply the Lotion
home.step2.p: Pump 2–3 times and massage evenly into skin. Ideal for morning use on large areas.
home.step3.title: Apply the Cream
home.step3.p: Use on thicker plaques or as an overnight treatment for intensive repair.
home.sci.label: The Science
home.sci.sub: ALFURIN isn't just skincare. It's the topical expression of PRC0028, AlsysLife's Phase III biologic that targets the S100 protein overexpression at the root of psoriatic inflammation.
home.sci1.p: In Phase III trials, 72% of patients achieved a PASI-75 response — a clinical benchmark for significant skin clearance — within 16 weeks of treatment.
home.sci2.p: Unlike downstream cytokine blockers, ALFURIN acts at the S100 protein level — switching off the inflammatory signal at its source for more durable results.
home.sci3.p: Developed and clinically validated by AlsysLife with 1,200+ patients enrolled across global trial sites following ICH-GCP international standards.

meta.psoriasis.title: ALFURIN | Understanding Psoriasis
meta.psoriasis.desc: Psoriasis is a chronic autoimmune disorder affecting millions worldwide. Learn about symptoms, types, and advanced treatment approaches from AlsysLife.
psoriasis.hero.label: Disease Area
psoriasis.hero.p: A comprehensive overview of psoriasis — its causes, symptoms, types, and the latest advances in therapeutic management.
psoriasis.what.label: Overview
psoriasis.what.p1: Psoriasis is a chronic autoimmune disorder that accelerates the lifecycle of skin cells, causing inflammation, redness, scaling, and irritation. The condition affects millions of individuals worldwide and can significantly impact physical, emotional, and social well-being.
psoriasis.what.p2: Unlike temporary skin conditions, psoriasis is driven by immune system dysfunction that triggers excessive skin cell production. Although the exact cause remains complex, genetics, environmental factors, infections, stress, and immune abnormalities all contribute to disease progression.
psoriasis.what.p3: The condition is characterized by periods of flares and remission, and its severity ranges from mild — with small patches — to severe, covering large areas of the body. Psoriasis can also affect the joints, leading to a form called psoriatic arthritis.
psoriasis.visual.label: People Affected Worldwide
psoriasis.sym.label: Signs & Symptoms
psoriasis.sym.sub: Symptoms can vary depending on the type and severity of the condition. People living with psoriasis may experience any combination of the following.
psoriasis.sym.1: Red, inflamed patches of skin with a well-defined border
psoriasis.sym.2: Thick silvery-white scales overlying raised plaques
psoriasis.sym.3: Persistent itching, burning sensation, and soreness
psoriasis.sym.4: Dry or cracked skin that may bleed
psoriasis.sym.5: Swollen, stiff joints in cases of psoriatic arthritis
psoriasis.sym.7: Emotional distress, anxiety, and reduced quality of life
psoriasis.sym.9: Skin lesions in sensitive areas (scalp, genitals, folds)
psoriasis.types.label: Classification
psoriasis.types.sub: Psoriasis presents in several distinct clinical forms, each with unique characteristics, distribution patterns, and treatment considerations.
psoriasis.type1.p: The most common form, affecting approximately 80–90% of patients. Characterized by raised, inflamed red lesions covered with silvery-white scales. Plaques typically appear on elbows, knees, scalp, and lower back.
psoriasis.type2.p: Presents as small, drop-shaped lesions (2–10mm) scattered across the trunk, arms, and legs. Often triggered by bacterial infections, particularly streptococcal throat infections, especially in children and young adults.
psoriasis.type3.p: Appears in body folds such as the armpits, groin, under the breasts, and around the genitals. Presents as smooth, red, inflamed patches rather than scaly plaques. Friction and sweating can aggravate symptoms.
psoriasis.type4.p: A severe form involving white pustules (blisters of non-infectious pus) surrounded by red, inflamed skin. Can be localized to the palms and soles (palmoplantar) or widespread across the body (generalized).
psoriasis.type5.p: A rare but potentially life-threatening form that affects large portions of the body simultaneously with widespread inflammation and exfoliation. Requires urgent medical attention and hospitalization in severe cases.
psoriasis.type6.p: A chronic inflammatory arthritis affecting up to 30% of psoriasis patients. Causes pain, swelling, and stiffness in joints along with skin symptoms. Can lead to permanent joint damage if left untreated.
psoriasis.treat.label: Therapeutic Management
psoriasis.treat.p1: Modern psoriasis management has been transformed by advances in immunology and molecular biology. Treatment selection depends on disease severity, affected body areas, patient history, and comorbidities.
psoriasis.treat.p2: At AlsysLife, we are dedicated to discovering innovative therapeutic solutions capable of improving long-term patient outcomes and restoring confidence to individuals living with chronic inflammatory skin diseases.
psoriasis.treat.p3: Our research into natural product-derived biologics and small molecule inhibitors targets the specific immune pathways responsible for psoriasis, aiming to deliver first-in-class therapies with superior safety profiles.
psoriasis.cta.p: AlsysLife is committed to developing next-generation therapies that address the unmet needs of psoriasis patients worldwide.

research.targets.label: Molecular Targets
research.targets.sub: Our research focuses on proteins and signaling pathways that drive the key hallmarks of psoriasis and autoimmune skin disease.
research.t1.p: S100A8 and S100A9 are key antimicrobial proteins overexpressed in psoriatic skin lesions. Our drug candidates target these proteins to disrupt the pro-inflammatory cascade that drives disease progression.
research.t2.p: Interleukin-6 is a pleiotropic cytokine with a central role in systemic inflammation. Our local IL-6 modulation approach aims to achieve therapeutic efficacy while minimizing systemic side effects.
research.t3.p: Tumor Necrosis Factor-alpha is a master regulator of systemic inflammation. Our next-generation TNF-α inhibitors build on established mechanisms while improving selectivity and tolerability profiles.
research.t4.p: Next-generation small molecule inhibitors targeting key cell signaling pathways involved in keratinocyte proliferation and immune cell activation — the fundamental drivers of psoriatic disease.
research.cta.p: We welcome scientific collaborations and research partnerships with leading institutions worldwide.
meta.science.title: ALFURIN | The Science — From Bark to Cream
meta.science.desc: Discover the plant science behind ALFURIN — a single bark extract from Limonia acidissima, independently patch-tested and dermatologically validated.
science.s1.label: THE ORIGIN
science.s1.p: The heart of Alfurin is a single plant extract – drawn only from the bark of the Indian wood apple tree (Limonia acidissima). See where it comes from.
science.s2.label: THE STORY
science.s2.p: Deep in tropical forests grows the Indian wood apple tree, Limonia acidissima. For Alfurin, only its bark is harvested – carefully removed and taken to the facility, where it becomes a plant extract. That extract is the active heart of this gentle care cream for skin prone to psoriasis. A good story deserves good care – here's how gentle Alfurin is on the skin.
science.s2.c1.p: Only the bark of Limonia acidissima is harvested – the tree stays standing.
science.s2.c2.p: The bark is pressed into a plant extract – the active heart of the formula.
science.s2.c3.p: The extract is blended into a gentle, steroid-free care cream.
science.s3.label: SKIN COMPATIBILITY
science.s3.p: Alfurin's skin compatibility was assessed in an independent, dermatologist-supervised patch test on 50 volunteers, including 25 with a history of allergies. No irritation or reactions were observed, and the cream was classified in the mildest, 'non-irritating' category. Read the full patch test below.
science.s4.label: CARE & RESEARCH
science.s4.p: Alfurin is a 100% plant-based, steroid-free care cream built around a single active – the bark extract of the Indian wood apple. It's made to soothe the look and feel of dryness, flaking and redness on skin prone to psoriasis, as part of a gentle daily routine. Its skin compatibility and everyday use have been looked at under recognised research standards (Declaration of Helsinki, GCP).
science.s4.disclaimer: Alfurin is a cosmetic product for the care of skin prone to psoriasis. It does not replace medical diagnosis or treatment.
